sections: Choose an appetite-sized route

Old Delhi is a poor place to arrive with a challenge to eat ten dishes. A better first food walk has a small snack, one proper meal and a sweet if you still want it. The lanes and the pauses between them are part of the visit, not inconvenient gaps between famous counters. Choose the order around the actual places you want to reach. Natraj in Chandni Chowk, Karim's near Jama Masjid and a named Kuremal outlet are possible anchors, but they are not three doors on the same block. Check each current location and leave enough time to move through crowded streets without hurrying.
Natraj: begin with one plate

Natraj Dahi Bhalle Wala is associated with dahi bhalla and aloo tikki. The contrast is useful: soft lentil dumplings with curd and chutneys, or a potato preparation with a different texture. Ask what is being served that day and choose one rather than ordering both automatically before a full meal. Chaat can combine dairy, spices and several toppings. If an ingredient matters to you, ask before the plate is assembled. A popular counter is not a guarantee about every allergy or preparation method. Watch the serving conditions and move on if you are not comfortable, without feeling that you have failed an essential stop.
Karim's: make room for the meal

Karim's original Old Delhi address is in Gali Kababian near Jama Masjid. Its own menu identity includes kebabs, korma and tandoori cooking. For a first visit, select a main dish and bread that work for the group, leaving the huge tasting spread for a larger table with the appetite to match. Clarify the meat and portion before ordering, especially if a dish name is unfamiliar. Ask about the current menu rather than treating an old account of the restaurant as a list of what will be available now. A family history can give the meal context, but it cannot tell you whether you will enjoy every dish.
A kulfi finish needs an exact shop

Kuremal is a name you will encounter in Old Delhi's kulfi search, including businesses using different full names. Kuremal Mohanlal lists a Chawri Bazar outlet in Kucha Pati Ram; Kuremal Mahavir Prasad also operates under the Kuremal name. Confirm the full business and location rather than assuming all similarly named pins are the same shop. Fruit-filled and other kulfi varieties can make a memorable final choice, but availability is seasonal and shop-specific. Ask about milk, nuts and the fruit preparation if those details matter. You can share a portion or stop without dessert. A food walk does not become better simply by leaving you uncomfortably full.
Keep the city in the visit

If you also plan to visit Jama Masjid, separate the worship-space visit from the meal and check its current access instructions. Do not carry the assumption that restaurant access establishes mosque access. Keep food and photography respectful of the places and people around you. Use a small bag, drink safe water and leave room to pause. Check the final bill and the merchant name before paying, and keep the next stop optional. Old Delhi's food is best encountered with curiosity and a little restraint, not with a stopwatch and a requirement to like everything.
Shyam Sweets: a Chawri Bazaar breakfast choice

Shyam Sweets' own site gives an address at 112 Chawri Bazar, and The Indian Express's food reporting describes its breakfast tradition. Choose a modest breakfast here instead of adding it after a full meal. Ask what is being prepared fresh that morning and order a small portion first. A historical food feature does not establish today's opening time, price or an unlimited ability to accommodate a large group.
Paranthe Wali Gali: choose one shop and one appetite

Delhi Tourism includes Paranthe Wali Gali in its food-tour material. Treat the lane as a choice among businesses, not one restaurant with a uniform menu or hygiene standard. Ask how a paratha is cooked and what the filling and accompaniments contain, and be realistic about a rich fried meal in a long tasting day. You do not need to eat at several counters to have experienced the lane.
Qureshi: resolve the exact kebab shop

Delhi Tourism has a specific listing for Abdul Ghani Qureshi Kabab Corner. Use the full name and actual location when confirming a visit, because similar Qureshi names do not establish the same business. Ask what meat is used, how the portion is served and whether the counter is operating when you plan to arrive. Keep a busy working lane clear and do not turn the grill into an obstacle for customers.
Changezi Chicken: a meal stop, not another snack

Changezi Chicken's own site identifies its Old Delhi restaurant and its named chicken preparation. If that is your priority, make room for a proper meal and confirm the exact branch, portion and current service. Do not add a second full meat meal after Karim's simply to complete a list. Ask about dairy, nuts and heat rather than assuming that the name tells you every ingredient.
Kuremal: distinguish similarly named kulfi businesses

The checked sites include Kuremal Mahavir Prasad Kulfiwale and a separate Kuremal branch directory associated with Mohan Lal. Do not treat their names, branches and products as interchangeable. Choose the exact business and address, then ask about the current fruit, dairy ingredients, portion and refrigeration. A stuffed-fruit image does not prove that a particular flavour is in season or suitable for an allergy.
Sita Ram Diwan Chand: a separate Paharganj choice

The operator's location page identifies its Chuna Mandi, Paharganj address. This is a concrete chole-bhature alternative, not a stop inside the same small Chawri Bazaar circuit. Choose it instead of another large breakfast if that is the food you want. Confirm the actual branch and current service, and allow for transport. Similar brand names and delivery pages are not enough to settle which counter you will visit.
Rajinder Da Dhaba: another neighbourhood, another meal

Rajinder Da Dhaba's own story page gives a Safdarjung Enclave DDA Market address. It is a separate dinner direction from the Old Delhi walk, not the final nearby stop on a tasting lane. Check current service and the exact ordering or seating format. If you want to go, keep the afternoon food light and plan the return. Do not promise a late-night opening simply because an older food crawl labels it that way.
Make the self-guided route smaller than the city

For a manageable morning, choose Shyam Sweets or another breakfast, one Old Delhi walk and a small dessert if wanted. For a meal-led visit, choose Karim's or Changezi rather than both. Paharganj and Safdarjung are separate alternatives. CR Park, Kamla Nagar and Majnu Ka Tilla belong to other neighbourhood outings, not an obligation to cross Delhi repeatedly in one day. This guide does not claim that a multi-neighbourhood list is a tested 24-hour route or publish a guessed map.
Kamla Nagar: a separate chole-bhature choice

The Indian Express's reporting identifies Chache Di Hatti with chole bhature in Kamla Nagar. It is a separate neighbourhood meal lead, not part of a compact Old Delhi walking loop. Confirm current operation and plan transport if choosing it, rather than trying to eat several full breakfasts across the city. A historical feature is background, not a live opening or price guarantee.

sections: Begin with a small tasting

A Kolkata sweet counter can make every tray look like the right answer. Resist the large mixed box until you know what you enjoy. Start with one or two small choices and ask the seller to explain the difference between them. The tasting is the useful part, not the number of sweets in your bag. This is an introduction to a few familiar Bengali sweets, not a competition between shops. Recipes, textures and sizes vary. Judge the actual piece or serving offered to you rather than expecting one famous name to taste identical at every counter.
Sandesh is a good place to ask questions

Sandesh is closely associated with Kolkata's sweet tradition, with versions that vary in firmness, flavour and filling. Ask which one is soft, which is firmer and whether a seasonal ingredient is used. A short conversation can be more helpful than choosing the most decorated piece. The milk-based foundation matters if you avoid dairy, and nuts or other additions may matter for allergies. Do not assume that a plain-looking sweet has a simple ingredient list. Ask about the actual preparation and shared handling if your restriction is important.
Rasgulla brings a different texture

Rasgulla, also called rosogolla, offers the contrast of a soft sweet in syrup. Choose a small serving and give it time rather than immediately comparing it to every other dessert you know. The syrup and the texture are part of the experience together. A counter may also offer baked or flavoured variations. Ask whether you are buying the familiar syrup version or a different preparation. A recognisable word on a sign can cover more than one item, and it is easier to clarify before the box is packed.
Mishti doi changes the pace

Mishti doi is sweetened yogurt, often with a creamy texture and a gentle sourness underneath the sweetness. It can feel like a quieter finish after a meal or a contrast to a plate of sweets. Choose a serving you can eat soon and ask how it should be kept. A small pot is not automatically a travel-ready souvenir. Temperature and journey length matter for dairy desserts. If you are taking it away, get clear storage guidance from the shop and make sure you can follow it. Do not turn a pleasant tasting into a doubtful snack several hours later.
Buy a gift box with the journey in mind

Tell the seller when the sweets will be eaten and how you will travel. Ask which items suit that plan, how they should be stored and whether the package is likely to leak or crush. Get the names and ingredients of an unfamiliar assortment so the recipient does not have to guess. For travel outside India, check your destination's current food-import rules before buying dairy sweets as gifts. A sealed box is not permission to carry every food across a border. If the journey makes storage difficult, enjoy a smaller serving in Kolkata instead. The memory of a well-chosen taste can last longer than a box purchased only because it looked generous.
A Bhowanipore counter is a concrete starting point

Balaram Mullick & Radharaman Mullick's store page lists 2, Paddapukur Road, Jadubabur Bazar, Bhowanipore. Its catalogue separates sandesh, syrup sweets, baked sweets and dahi, among other categories. Use that as a specific lead for a small tasting rather than a declaration that one shop is the city's best. Confirm the outlet and current counter selection before travelling. A long online catalogue does not mean every sweet is available at every branch that day. Ask for one familiar preparation and one contrast that interests you, then choose a quantity you can eat or keep properly.
Traditional names and new preparations can coexist

The Balaram catalogue includes contemporary flavours and baked preparations alongside familiar Bengali sweet categories. Read the exact name and ask what has changed. A baked rosogolla, a flavoured sandesh and a plain syrup sweet are different purchases even when the name connects them. Let texture guide the comparison: a firmer piece, something softer, a sweet in syrup or a spoonful of doi. Do not assume the most decorated option is the most useful introduction. Ask about dairy, nuts and other additions, especially when a restriction matters; a flavour label is not a complete ingredient or cross-contact statement.
A canned sweet is a different travel decision

The site at kcdasonline.com lists canned rossogolla among its products. That is another format to consider when a loose syrup sweet would be awkward to carry, but packaging does not settle every travel question. Read the actual can's label, sealing, date and storage instructions, including what changes once it is opened. Confirm the seller and the specific product rather than assuming similarly named businesses or websites are interchangeable. This guide makes no claim about invention, exclusive origin or which counter is the authoritative version of a sweet. A clear product description matters more to this tasting than a disputed heritage story.
Keep the sweet stop separate from a full meal

If biryani or a Bengali lunch is already the main meal, do not make a large sweet-shop assortment another compulsory course. A small serving or a later tasting can be enough. Tell the counter staff when the sweets will be eaten and whether they need to survive a journey rather than asking only what is famous. For a gift, record the names and care instructions so the recipient is not left guessing. Ask the shop about the particular preparation's keeping requirements; neither a dry-looking surface nor a closed box establishes a safe shelf life. When your journey cannot support the required storage, enjoy the sweet in Kolkata instead of taking a doubtful parcel home.
Girish and Nakur: a named sandesh stop

Girish Chandra Dey and Nakur Chandra Nandy gives its address as 56 Ramdulal Sarkar Street and identifies sandesh as its specialism. Its catalogue ranges from karapak jalbhara to chocolate and fruit-named preparations. Use that range as a reason to ask what is fresh at the counter, not to assume every catalogue item is available. Compare a small traditional piece with a different preparation before buying a large box.
Balaram Mullick: verify the counter and the season

Balaram Mullick and Radharaman Mullick's current catalogue includes jalbhara, baked sweets, sandesh and mishti doi; its branch finder identifies a Bhowanipore counter on Paddapukur Road. Choose the exact branch first. Seasonal jaggery products and a year-round catalogue are not the same promise, so ask what is made that day and how it should be stored. For a gift box, get the maker's travel and refrigeration advice for the actual assortment.
Bhim Chandra Nag: a distinct heritage-shop lead

Conde Nast Traveller's Kolkata sweet-shop guide includes Bhim Chandra Nag among the city's established counters. Choose a small tasting based on what is fresh that day rather than buying a large box around a historical superlative. Confirm the exact counter and current opening directly if making a special journey. A shop's age does not establish which sweet will suit your taste or travel well.
Ganguram: choose the counter and the product

Ganguram-branded businesses maintain their own product and shop information, but the name alone should not stand in for an exact address. Check which counter you intend to visit and ask about the actual batch, ingredients and packing. A savoury snack, a fresh milk sweet and a packaged gift have different storage needs. Do not assume that every item shown online is stocked at every counter.
Chittaranjan: make the rosogolla stop a small one

Conde Nast Traveller identifies Chittaranjan Mistanna Bhandar with rosogolla and Madhuporko, a distinct sweet preparation. Use that as an editorial food lead and confirm current availability rather than copying its published hours as a promise. Ask for the smallest useful tasting and check milk, nut and flavour ingredients. If stock has finished, choose another fresh item or another day rather than treating a sold-out counter as a failed trip.
Hindusthan Sweets: verify the particular branch

Hindusthan Sweets maintains its own site, providing a direct source for a named alternative beyond a generic list of sweet types. Ask which branch has the preparation you want and whether it can be packed for your actual journey. Do not turn a photograph or a festival range into an everyday stock promise. Perishable dairy sweets need a realistic time and temperature plan after purchase.
Gupta Brothers: sweets and a vegetarian meal are separate choices

Gupta Brothers' Salt Lake site presents vegetarian food, sweets and snacks. Choose whether this is a tasting stop or a meal, and use that exact branch information rather than treating all similarly named counters as one location. Ask about current stock, ingredients and packaging. A broader menu can help a group with different appetites, but it does not establish an allergy-safe kitchen without a direct answer.

sections: Start with the item, then the market

Mumbai's markets are part of the city visit, but they need not become a shopping marathon. Decide whether you want a casual browse, a specific fabric or a small gift before choosing the area. That choice gives you something to compare and helps you recognise when the outing has given you enough. Colaba Causeway offers a browse that can fit a southern Mumbai day. The market areas around Crawford Market and Mangaldas Market offer another kind of visit, especially if textiles are the focus. Treat them as separate choices when your time is short. A map can show neighbouring markets, but it cannot tell you how long a careful purchase will take.
Colaba when the browse is part of the walk

Fit a Colaba Causeway browse around your waterfront or neighbourhood visit instead of travelling solely to collect a souvenir. Look at clothing, accessories or a small keepsake with the same care you would use at home. A low asking price does not make an item useful, and a seller's enthusiasm does not oblige you to buy. Try the practical checks first. Does the clasp work? Is the zip smooth? Is the stitching secure? For clothing, confirm the size and examine it rather than relying on a label alone. For an item described as antique or a designer product, do not treat the claim as established by its appearance. Ask what evidence supports it, and walk away if the answer does not satisfy you.
Mangaldas Market for a fabric-led visit

If textiles are what you want, make Mangaldas Market the centre of the outing. Begin with a rough idea of the use: a garment, a home textile or a piece to take back for later sewing. That matters because width, drape, care and quantity affect whether a fabric will work. A beautiful colour is only one part of the choice. Ask what the fabric is made of and how the price is measured. Compare the same length and width when comparing quotes, and make sure you understand whether finishing or tailoring is a separate charge. If you need an exact quantity for a garment, get the requirement from the person making it before buying. Extra metres are not automatically useful, and too little can make the whole purchase frustrating.
Make a market visit enjoyable even without a purchase

The wider Crawford Market area can be an interesting browse alongside the fabric search. Keep your bag close, choose a manageable walk and step aside when you need to check your phone. Do not block a narrow lane while deciding where to go next. A shopping district is also a workplace for the people moving through it. Give yourself permission to leave without buying. You can enjoy displays, buildings and the rhythm of trading without turning every conversation into a transaction. If a piece stays in your mind, you can compare it calmly with another option. Pressure is a poor way to choose something you will take home.
Pay for the exact thing you inspected

Before paying, inspect the actual item being packed, not only the sample shown during the conversation. Confirm the final total and any exchange terms. A fabric cut to your chosen length or an item altered for you may have different return conditions from a standard product; ask before the cutting or alteration happens. For a useful receipt, ask for the item and quantity to be recorded. Check the merchant on the payment screen, keep the confirmation and avoid repeating a pending payment before the status is clear. Finish with packing that protects the purchase and fits your journey. A good market find should be easy to enjoy after the trip as well as during it.
A souvenir with a use after the trip

A Mumbai keepsake need not be large or expensive to carry the memory of the city. Think first about where it will live: on a desk, in a kitchen, in a wardrobe or in someone else's home. A useful notebook, a small textile or a light everyday bag can be easier to enjoy than a fragile object chosen only because it looked striking at the counter. For a city-specific gift, check the material as carefully as the motif. The Bombay Store's current souvenir catalogue, for example, identifies Mumbai-themed magnets made from MDF as well as diaries and other small items. That is a useful distinction: a printed city design tells you what the object depicts, not whether it is wood, metal, handmade or locally produced. Buy the stated material and workmanship, not the story you imagined from the appearance.
A fixed-price stop at The Bombay Store

The Bombay Store's own location page lists its Fort shop in Western India House on Sir P. M. Road. Its catalogue gives a starting point for looking at smaller gifts such as bookmarks, tote bags, diaries and souvenirs before going. This is a different shopping format from a street-market negotiation and can fit a gift-led visit when you want to compare labelled items more calmly. An online catalogue is not a branch stock list. If you want one particular design, check with the shop before making a special journey. Inspect the piece you will receive, ask for care instructions and confirm exchange terms before paying. Do not use the existence of a recognised retailer as a reason to skip those checks, especially for something fragile or intended for shipping.
Choose a textile as a textile, not a vague souvenir

A fabric length from Mangaldas Market and a finished accessory from a gift shop solve different needs. For a fabric length, decide who will make or use it and how much is required. For a finished item, examine seams, fastening and care. If a seller names a weaving tradition or a place of origin, ask how that claim is documented instead of treating a pattern as proof. A Paithani purchase deserves its own questions about weave, origin and use; it is not just another colourful item in a souvenir bag. Likewise, a textile described as handwoven should have a clear explanation of the material and technique. Keep any description on the receipt when it is important to the decision. The right purchase is one you understand well enough to care for at home.
Old, antique and decorative are different claims

Markets can tempt a traveller with metalware, old-looking objects and curious decoration. A dark surface or worn edge does not establish age, and an age claim does not establish a lawful export. Ask what the seller is actually selling: a modern decorative piece, a used object or an item claimed to have historical value. If the claim matters and the paperwork is unclear, leave the item rather than guessing the rules. Any purchase presented as an antiquity needs a separate check of the current legal requirements before payment or shipment. A contemporary decorative object with a clear description can be a more straightforward gift, but material, packing and destination restrictions still deserve attention.
Pack the purchase before you leave the counter

Compare gifts by weight, size and how they will travel as well as by price. Ask for padding around a fragile piece and separate items that can scratch each other. For something made from a natural material, or for food, check the destination's current import rules instead of assuming a small gift is exempt. If the shop offers shipping, establish the final shipping charge, destination details and what happens if the parcel is damaged before agreeing. Keep the item description and receipt with the order record. For a gift carried in your bag, leave enough room to protect it properly. A well-chosen keepsake should add a memory to the trip, not an awkward parcel problem on the way home.
Chor Bazaar: inspect the object, not the antique story

Travel + Leisure Asia includes Chor Bazaar among Mumbai's browsing markets, with furniture, old objects and film-related decor. Choose it for an object-led browse, not a guarantee of genuine antiques. Ask about material, repairs, provenance, export restrictions and packing before paying. An old-looking finish does not establish age, and a seller's story is not a certificate. Take measurements and leave large or fragile purchases behind if shipping is unresolved.
Dadar Flower Market: a working wholesale setting

The same editorial guide identifies Dadar's flower market as a separate shopping experience. Visit to observe or buy flowers while allowing traders and deliveries to move. Ask before close photographs of workers and avoid blocking a passage for a portrait. Flowers are perishable and may be unsuitable to take across borders, so buy only what you can use locally. Do not promise a fixed sunrise scene or price from an older feature.
Hill Road and Linking Road: a fashion browse, not a provenance claim

Travel + Leisure Asia identifies these Bandra shopping areas as distinct street-market options. Choose one with an idea of fit, budget and what you need, and inspect each item before paying. A low price or familiar logo does not establish authenticity, ethical production or local manufacture. Ask about exchanges and check seams, fastenings and sizing in person. There is no need to buy simply because bargaining is expected.
Santacruz West: a fabric-led alternative

LBB identifies the Station Road market in Santacruz West with fabric shopping. Choose it when cloth is your aim rather than expecting the same experience as Colaba's souvenir browse. Confirm the shop, fibre, width, price unit and care instructions before cutting. A fabric purchase for tailoring also needs time for the actual sewing and fitting. The guide's transit label is not enough to establish a current metro route; check the journey independently.
Weekly and arts markets need a real date

Kala Ghoda Association publishes dated festival programmes, not evidence of a permanent weekly craft bazaar. Use the organiser's current calendar for an actual event and do not assume a past programme is running today. This guide has not verified a standing Juhu Beach Sunday flea market from the sources checked, so it is not a dependable Sunday-shopping plan. Choose an established shopping area or a specifically confirmed event instead.
Choose souvenirs by material and travel rules

Film posters, chappals, brassware, embroidery, soap, spices and small vehicle models are different purchases, not a single Mumbai-authenticity test. Ask who made the item and where, inspect it and consider its use after the trip. For Warli-labelled work, ask about the artist and attribution instead of treating a motif as proof of tribal authorship. Check destination customs rules for food, plant, animal or antique materials before buying, and keep a receipt with a precise description.
sources: Travel + Leisure Asia: Mumbai market selection

sections: Choose the kind of evening

Bukhara and Indian Accent offer different reasons to plan a Delhi dinner. One centres a North-West Frontier-inspired, tandoor-led identity; the other describes inventive Indian cooking using global ingredients and techniques. Neither needs to be declared the universal winner. Begin with the food and the occasion. Do you want to share breads and selected dishes, or spend time with a more structured menu? Make that choice before letting awards or a difficult reservation decide what you are hungry for.
Bukhara: breads, tandoor and its dal

Bukhara at ITC Maurya describes dishes such as Dal Bukhara, tandoor-cooked meats and vegetables, and Naan Bukhara. These explain the restaurant’s established direction without turning a brand’s own praise into a first-hand verdict. Ask about portions and choose a meal that fits the group. A few shared dishes can make more sense than one famous item per person. Vegetarian options are part of the description, but specific requirements and cross-contact still need discussion with the restaurant.
Indian Accent: a different menu language

Indian Accent’s New Delhi page places it at The Lodhi on Lodhi Road and describes both à la carte and a chef’s tasting menu. Its approach connects Indian flavours with ingredients and techniques from elsewhere, making it a different proposal from a straightforward tandoor meal. Check the current menu and the format available for your service. A tasting menu, optional pairing and à la carte order are different commitments of time and money. Ask whether the whole table needs the same format and how dietary changes are handled.
The reservation is part of the choice

Confirm the exact venue, service, party size and booking terms. These are hotel restaurants at different addresses, not adjacent stops for a casual food crawl. Plan the journey and leave enough time to arrive without turning dinner into a traffic deadline. Ask about deposits, cancellation and any minimum or menu requirements before reserving. A booking confirmation does not automatically include drinks, a pairing or every item mentioned on a restaurant page. Dress and age requirements should also come from current restaurant information.
Compare the complete meal

Use the current food price, likely drinks, taxes and any applicable charges to compare the evening. A headline menu number is not the final bill. Expensive does not mean personally right, and a familiar signature does not mean every diner will want the same order. Choose Bukhara for its stated tandoor-led direction, or Indian Accent for its stated inventive menu approach, when that is the evening you want. Keep the final details with the restaurant. The aim is a meal you chose knowingly, not a photograph proving you visited a famous name.
Alkauser: a kebab-led alternative

Alkauser's own site describes its Kakori kebab tradition. Choose it for a kebab-led meal and confirm the exact outlet, current menu and seating rather than assuming an older Chanakyapuri recommendation identifies today's branch. Ask about meat, ingredients and portion size. The operator's family history is its own account, not independent proof of every origin claim.
Moti Mahal: keep the restaurant and origin claims separate

A current third-party listing identifies Moti Mahal in Daryaganj. That gives a specific restaurant lead, not proof of a disputed claim about who invented butter chicken. Choose the actual food, branch and setting, and check current service directly. Do not confuse similarly named restaurant groups or use a historical superlative as a reason to ignore the menu and total bill.
Kallu Nihari: confirm a narrow food plan

A current Zomato listing identifies Kallu Nihari in Daryaganj. Use it as a third-party lead and confirm the actual counter, service and availability directly, especially if one dish is the whole reason for the journey. A slow-cooked preparation can sell out, and a general listing does not establish a particular serving time. Ask about meat and richness, and make it the meal rather than another compulsory tasting after dinner.
